meaning_derived_from_sources: SEC policy/trigger responsibility is distinct from each recipient's own state and execution; SEC009 is conditional on relevant selected operation/recipient scope, not a requirement that every recipient capability or all mechanisms be complete.

For a selected recipient, compare the selected phase and its evidence separately: instruction/dispatch, receipt, actual application with post-state/isolation, and recovery. A later phase is not presumed from an earlier one; future receipt/application/recovery is not a universal dispatch prerequisite.

Class violation denotes a source-grounded contradiction or observed failure against the obligation (for example conflicting binding/actions, prohibited expansion, continuing after stop, non-delivery/non-application, or incomplete recovery). Class unknown denotes missing, unresolved, unobserved, or insufficient evidence; it does not assert a contradiction.
Do not spread an unknown or stop to unrelated valid scope. Keep safety-trigger/external-effect unknown bound to the affected identity; general meaning unknown alone does not establish a global stop.
No success/pass class is specified in the L4 code_classes map. No class for unlisted codes is derived; use unknown pending source authority.

approved_requirement_links.meaning: 初回scopeに必要な条件付き停止契約。SEC owns policy/trigger; each recipient owns its state/execution. Limit closure to required selected scope; identify required closure separately from unselected/unobserved items.

Tie revoke/scope drift/uncertain external effect/credential leak/abnormal communication/runtime deviation to operation and recipient identities; propagate to all applicable recipients; distinguish delivery, application and non-observation; a new stop does not establish in-flight success.

Keep safety/external-effect unknown local to affected identity, avoid globalizing unrelated general-meaning unknown, preserve a recoverable pre-state and distinguish receipt from actual application/recovery.
